title: Progressive Ramp & Safety Gates — Rollouts Prototype and UX Review
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Prototype a progressive traffic ramp UI for Rollouts that combines percentage-based scheduling, time-based ramps, automated safety gates, and one-click rollback. Goals: 1) Make it easy for engineers and PMs to create canary/A-B experiments with predictable traffic curves. 2) Surface risk with clear safety gates and simulated traffic preview. 3) Provide cost and latency projections per split. 4) Ensure accessibility and keyboard-first controls.

What this ticket contains: finalized mid-fidelity screens, interactive Figma prototype link, accessibility checklist, dev handoff tokens, and a short report from 5 usability sessions. This design emphasizes explicit "hold" steps (stepwise holds), confidence thresholds, automatic rollback triggers, and an undo stack for quick recovery. Also includes a YAML export option for infra teams to reuse rollout specs in CI/CD.

Success metrics: reduce time-to-create rollout by 35%, reduce rollout rollback incidence by 20% through clearer safety gates, and increase confidence-to-launch (self-reported) by +1.0 on a 5-point scale in usability tests.
acceptance_criteria: Design screens include: create rollout, edit ramp steps, safety gate config, simulated traffic preview, metric diff view, cost projection per split, and rollback flow.
Interactive prototype demonstrates: time-based ramp, manual step holds, automatic rollback when metric threshold exceeded, and YAML export.
Accessibility: All controls reachable via keyboard, ARIA labels for sliders and split inputs, color contrast passes AA, and screen-reader flow documented.
Engineering handoff includes design tokens, motion specs, and a small test checklist for end-to-end QA (create -> apply -> observe metrics -> trigger rollback).
PM/Eng sign-off obtained and implementation estimate validated with ENG-4028.
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Initial concept sketches uploaded. Focused on 'progressive ramp' as primary mental model — linear vs exponential ramp presets and a custom curve editor. Shared with PM and Eng for early feedback.

2026-02-22 Marcus Liu (eng): Liking the time-based ramp. Constraint: backend only supports up to 6 discrete steps for now; suggested we provide an abstraction layer (preset curves) and limit the curve editor to produce <= 6 effective steps.

2026-02-27 Julia Ke (PM): Added requirements for cost projection per split and integration with existing alerting (canary-alerts). Requested a simulated traffic preview that shows expected QPS per variant.

2026-03-03 Usability: Ran 5 moderated tests with platform engineers. Key findings: participants expected an automatic hold at key thresholds, confusion between instantaneous % edits vs scheduled ramp. Action: add explicit 'Add hold' CTA and preview timeline that shows hold points.

2026-03-05 Design update: Implemented 'safety gates' panel with three trigger types: metric threshold, time hold, and manual approval. Added inline help copy and link to runbook. Updated Figma prototype.

2026-03-07 Accessibility review (Indira Shah): Suggested ARIA roles for the slider and that percentage inputs accept keyboard increments of 0.1%. Also recommended a non-visual timeline summary for screen readers.

2026-03-09 Marcus Liu (eng): Reviewed dev tokens and motion specs. Confirmed feasibility for simulated traffic preview using existing load-projection API (ENG-5091). Minor change: round projected costs to cents to avoid noisy decimals.

2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Pushed final prototype link and confluence doc. Requesting Design Review and sign-off from PM and Eng. Created GH PR for static assets: #2789. Next: implement canary overlay metrics in console dashboards (follow-up ticket).
